bug_semantics: Anyquery server mode binds a MySQL-wire TCP listener and forwards client SQL to the backing SQLite connection with no SQLITE_ATTACH authorizer. SQLite ATTACH DATABASE (and VACUUM INTO, which SQLite implements as attach) creates or overwrites a file at an attacker-chosen path. The Vitess/MySQL rewriter treats ATTACH as unparsable MySQL and, on StmtUnknown, runs the original statement against SQLite. Default auth is AuthServerNone when AuthFile/Users are empty, so an unauthenticated mysql client can write arbitrary files (cron, webroot PHP, authorized_keys) wherever the process can write, enabling AFW and environment-dependent RCE. Affected through 0.4.4; 0.4.5 installs a sandbox authorizer that denies non-memory ATTACH unless --allow-attach plus allowed dirs.
flaw_origin: The MySQL compatibility layer commit 90e7eaa8f3d7cc4b4dffa3fb4ac111284a8e81ab (2024-05-27) first wrote the network SQL proxy: MySQLServer.Start() with AuthServerNone, handler.ComQuery/runSimpleQuery doing DB.Query(client SQL), and getQueryType swallowing MySQL parse errors so SQLite-only ATTACH is executed as-is. Parent e01a128eb5d7da13b20bcfe8ae591ff35d11115a has no namespace/mysql*.go. Later 3993837954bf7e23de54703d740ee76f6df02a59 only wired the existing MySQLServer into `anyquery server`; it did not first-write the proxy. No commit-object AI marker on the BIC.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-xrcf-6jh3-ggvx / CVE-2026-50006 is a real, vendor-acknowledged missing-authorization bug, not a withdrawn advisory. Server mode speaks the MySQL protocol, defaults to accepting any connection, and executes client SQL on SQLite. ATTACH DATABASE is a native SQLite file-create primitive; the MySQL rewriter intentionally forwards unparsable (SQLite-only) statements, so ATTACH reaches the engine and writes attacker-chosen paths.
